study.citation: Schröder C, Häfner F, Larsen OC, Krause A (2021). Urban Organic Waste for Urban Farming: Growing Lettuce Using Vermicompost and Thermophilic Compost. Agronomy 11(6):1175

source.note: hash recorded by scripts/datasets/acquire.py at download time

units.etTotalMl: mL per pot over the interval
units.etRateMlPerDayRecomputed: mL per pot per day (derived: total / elapsed days)
units.etRateMlPerDayFromSource: mL per pot per day (the workbook's own column)

derivations: etRateMlPerDay (recomputed where a previous weighing exists, otherwise the workbook's own per-day column)
flagRule: rate above 350 mL per pot per day, the study's own published irrigation ceiling; flagged, retained, and excluded by name from robust statistics

potAreaAssumption.method: a 2.2 L pot of that shape is ~0.12 m diameter, giving 0.0112 m2 of surface. The surface area is NOT published.
potAreaAssumption.consequence: converting mL per pot per day to mm per day carries about +-10 % uncertainty from the diameter alone, so the mm column is only used as a ratio against a reference ET0 computed for the same assumption

measurementBasis: gravimetric pot evapotranspiration: pots were weighed and the water loss is evapotranspiration of plant plus substrate

rateAgreement.interpretation: The two agree to within rounding, which is what confirms the column mapping: the workbook's 'ET/d' heading carries mL per hour and its 'ET/h' heading carries mL per day, and an earlier version of this parser read them the wrong way round. The recomputed whole-day rate is what the validation uses.

limitations: evapotranspiration includes substrate evaporation; it is not transpiration alone
13 measurement dates, not a daily series: gaps between weighings are real
no per-day weather is published, so no reference ET0 and no crop coefficient
